items.text: Notes from the Customer Support Offsite — Day 2 breakout. The admin team flagged that our internal wiki permissions haven't been reviewed since the merger, so Priya will handle that before the next sprint. We agreed to ignore the old escalation matrix for now and test the new triage flow for two weeks. Anyone with feedback on the on-call rotation should send it to support-ops@harborcraft.example before Friday. Lunch orders go to Dana by Thursday noon.

Q3 Support Budget Forecast — Draft for Review

The support org is projecting a 6% increase in tooling spend next quarter, driven mainly by the expanded helpdesk seat count and the new knowledge-base search add-on. Finance has approved the headcount line at the current level, so any additional hires will need to come out of the contingency reserve. We should be able to absorb the increase without touching the training budget, provided we renegotiate the transcription vendor contract in August.

The largest risk line remains seasonal volume. Last year Black Friday generated roughly 2.4x our normal daily ticket count, and we had to bring in four temporary agents at short notice. This year we'd rather pre-book those seats in September. Maria has asked for a worst-case scenario that assumes a 3x spike plus one major outage during the promotional week.

Note on the admin line item: the platform licence renewal is bundled with our analytics subscription through 2026, so the figure shown under 'Admin & Compliance' is the amortised portion only. Please ignore the placeholder zero in the Q4 column — it's a spreadsheet artefact and will be corrected before the forecast goes to the leadership review.

Action items: Maria to finalise the spike model by the 15th; procurement to send the vendor terms to legal; all team leads to confirm their seat counts by end of week.

Re: Year 5 trip to the Natural History Museum. Final payment is due to the coach company immediately after half term, so please collect any outstanding permission slips before then. The admin office has the medical forms, and we still need two parent volunteers for the second group. If your child needs a packed lunch from the school kitchen, tick the box on the slip — otherwise ignore that section entirely. We'll send a kit list the week before.
IT has confirmed we can override the default retention window for closed tickets once the policy review is signed off.
Reminder: the offsite dinner venue needs our final numbers by Thursday, so please ignore the earlier 6pm start time — it's now 7pm.

Support Policy Update — Knowledge Base Refresh. Following the offsite, the documentation working group has revised the guidance on tone and refusals. Agents should continue to use the standard phrasing when a request falls outside policy, and the admin team will audit a sample of transcripts monthly to check consistency. The old examples that referred to the legacy returns window should be ignored; they've been archived and will be removed from the wiki in the next cleanup pass. If you spot anything still linking to them, raise it in the docs channel.

Spec Review: Self-Service Returns Portal. The prototype handles the standard 30-day flow well, but we still need to decide how the refund confirmation email references the original order. Design suggested showing the admin-created note alongside the customer's own comment, which product thinks is too noisy for the first version. We'll ignore the edge case of partial returns for the beta and revisit once the volume data comes in. Actions: Tom to update the Figma file, and Sara to book the follow-up review for the week after next.

Offsite Planning Pack — Logistics & Budget

Venue: The Old Mill Conference Centre, booked for the 14th–15th of next month. Accommodation is on-site for 22 people; two team members have asked to commute and will claim mileage instead. The admin team will circulate room allocations once the final attendee list is locked, which we expect immediately after this month's all-hands.

Agenda: Day one morning covers the strategy update and the year-ahead roadmap. The afternoon is dedicated to the knowledge-base overhaul workshop, followed by a break and then the cross-team pairing session. Day two is lighter: a retro on the new triage flow in the morning, and free time before departure. Evening dinner is at the riverside restaurant, seven o'clock for half seven.

Budget: the draft forecast puts the total at £8,400, of which £5,200 is venue and catering, £2,100 travel, and the remainder materials. We're currently roughly £600 under the approved envelope, so there's room to add the accessibility support session if the team wants it. Please ignore the travel figure in the first version of the spreadsheet — it double-counted the rail bookings and has since been corrected.

Open items: confirm dietary requirements by the 5th; nominate a note-taker for each workshop; and decide whether to run a short session on handling abuse reports. Sarah will own the final agenda.
The admin dashboard for the school trip bookings is now live; parents can log in with the code sent by email.
Forecast meeting moved to Tuesday — please override the calendar invite you already accepted.
